scope: All three downloaded originals were actually opened using image viewing. This is reference review before model renders, not completed-model acceptance.

photos.author: Pyzhou
observations: View from southwest shows broad chamfered southwest corner with vertical store letters; Moxing Tower lies at far southeast end of long Nanjing frontage, not over the near corner.
Pale warm stone/plaster walls, horizontal rustication on large corner/vertical piers, dark rectangular window groups, deep horizontal cornices and brackets are visible.
Lower large columns span more than one window level; lower projected balcony carries stone balustrades, while higher continuous balcony/individual portions use dark metal rails.
Near south/west corner has paired scroll/capital details and broken curved pediment motifs. Long facade is articulated into repeated groups, not a plain uniform window grid.
A tower can be seen distantly but its lower stage is partly masked; use closer photographs for tower morphology.
Street trees/signboards/people obscure lower storefronts. Roof interior and rear elevations are unobserved. Photo is unsuitable for deriving complete width/depth or surveyed heights.

photos.author: Livelikerw
observations: View from southeast street junction clearly identifies the Moxing Tower above the southeast chamfered entrance corner; long Nanjing facade extends left, Zhejiang-side face extends right/back.

A wide chamfered/stepped clock base carries one visible circular dial; above it are a broad square pavilion with arched opening and exterior columns, a smaller squared or chamfered pavilion with arched opening and slender columns, then a small open circular colonnade.

Round lantern cap is shallow/curved with concentric moulded rings and small top neck; a tall thin rod with transverse elements continues above it. Lower pavilions have strong projecting entablatures/dentils and decorative arch surrounds.

Main corner entrance facade below tower contains a tall arched central opening, small dark metal balcony, paired giant columns/pilasters and large broken/raised curved pediment with central relief/cartouche.
A large FANCL advertisement wraps the high chamfered corner below clock base. Its concealed original wall/window form cannot be verified from this photograph.

Zhejiang-side body north of the corner is not a full-depth equal-height box: a short high upper section steps down to a lower rear wing with large arched windows/openings. Exact transition distances/heights and relation to rear footprint are not measured.
Neighbor buildings on both sides of street are outside Sincere identity; they must not be incorporated simply because photographed together.

photos.author: Chainwit.
observations: Modern night close-up confirms southeast corner axial composition, projecting curved pediment, central arch, paired columns and dark metal balcony, with stone balustrade at lower level.
Clock base plus two square/chamfered pavilions and circular upper lantern remain visible; viewpoint foreshortens heights severely, so apparent vertical ratios are not survey dimensions.
Large MIDO advertisement conceals upper corner wall / roof edge; supporting frames and scaffold-like structures are visible. Do not infer exact windows beneath advertising.
Night colored lighting, illuminated letters and advertisements cannot establish daytime masonry color or original1917 appearance.
Capture metadata is2024-04-24; file upload2026-07-17 is not the photograph date. Modern signs differ from2013; references are multi-period.

source_metadata_note: Root downloaded tower and modern originals plus Commons pages; this reviewer read extra-photo-fetch.json and independently viewed image files. Original2010 Commons page was independently fetched/read by this reviewer.
height_and_scale_limits: No photograph supplies a surveyed width, depth, calibrated ground plane or total tower datum.
Official66m and61m describe street-front lengths; they do not verify a100×68m complete footprint.
Official30余米 body and3层空塔 are retained;51.3m authored total cannot be described as a documented or measured sum.
The apparent clockbase-plus-pavilion sequence is a visible component description; do not silently assert it equals the historical tower storey accounting.
recommended_required_features: Southeast tower at the junction; broad west/south chamfer is a different, untowered corner.
Long horizontal south facade with grouped giant columns, curved broken pediments, deep cornices, stone and dark-metal balconies.
Open tower archways/lantern, square-to-round decreasing tower stages, low curved cap and slender rod.
Zhejiang-side northern upper step-down / lower wing should either be represented cautiously or stated as a specific unmodeled/simplified limit.
unknown_or_estimated: Exact full boundary, courtyard arrangement and roof interior
Rear facades and partly hidden eastern-side structure
Structural floor datums, chamber heights and tower/rod end points
Detailed orders/capitals/cartouches, exact street bays and metalwork
